proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 2.1--2.2 identify the two-arm binary reduced experiment and Theorem 2.3 transfers its unrestricted minimax value exactly to a common bounded interval.
For two bounded-outcome arms, iid half assignment and a nonlinear endpoint-derived estimator attain the unrestricted minimax value characterized by a finite convex program.
Under the paper's permutation-invariant uncertainty class and linear-estimation formulation, complete randomization and a Neyman allocation solve the stated minimax problem.
For general multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and assignment mechanisms, the paper gives exact variance identities for linear unbiased estimators.
For multi-arm complete randomization with fixed limiting allocation proportions, regression-adjusted estimators admit regular design-based asymptotic comparisons.
Second-order asymptotic minimax behavior can be characterized by square completion and a problem-specific differential operator.
Restricted normal-mean minimax risk has a boundary-layer analysis based on least-favorable distributions.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population total estimation, pairwise-independent sampling and midpoint-differenced Horvitz--Thompson estimation attain the sharp minimax criterion.

prose_updates.tldr: For the fixed three-arm contrast \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\) and any common finite outcome interval \([L,U]\), an exact endpoint-transfer theorem makes the unrestricted and iid bounded minimax values \((U-L)^2\) times their binary values. The eight-type orbit game remains a literal reduction only for binary endpoint schedules. Its new field-level kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1'\), transfers it through the singular \(\eta=0\) fiber, and gives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier with penalty \(2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\). A Rao--Blackwellized bounded Airy rule and a rescaled endpoint complete-schedule prior attain the matching upper and lower expansions.

project_justification.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.1--2.3) give the two-arm reduced experiment and bounded endpoint transfer, while the accepted repository parent supplies the binary multi-arm orbit reduction. Neither source determines the three-arm half-wedge constant, controls its singular transverse fiber, derives its allocation frontier, or proves that the three-arm binary value transfers exactly to every common bounded interval.
project_justification.niche: For an active arm contrasted with the equally weighted average of two labelled comparators, zero-sum normalization permits an exact bounded endpoint transfer, while the binary endpoint adversary retains a genuinely three-arm half-wedge geometry and a nonregular \(\eta=0\) bridge absent from two-arm theory.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a design-preserving finite-\(n\) endpoint equality, derives the exact half-wedge Airy constant and singular finite-orbit bridge, constructs a Rao--Blackwellized bounded estimator and rescaled endpoint prior, and establishes the necessary-and-sufficient \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier with the squared-width risk scaling.

sampling_model.design: The unrestricted benchmark ranges over every law on \(\mathcal A^n\) chosen independently of the fixed complete schedule; no coordinate independence or arm positivity is imposed. The attaining comparator is iid \(q^\star\), and the allocation frontier ranges over iid triangular arrays \(q_n\).
sampling_model.units: There are \(n\) labelled units with a fixed complete schedule in \([L,U]^{3n}\), where \(-\infty<L<U<\infty\) is common to all arms and units and fixed with respect to \(n\). Binary schedules are the normalized endpoint subclass; no superpopulation sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives exactly one of three labelled arms and reveals only \(Y_i^{[L,U]}(A_i)\). The target is the fixed finite-population contrast with weights \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity restriction is imposed on unrestricted competing designs. Each iid frontier array is eventually interior because it converges to \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance regressions. The bounded upper rule independently Bernoulliizes normalized observed outcomes and then analytically averages that randomization, so the reported Rao--Blackwellized estimator is a deterministic function of the realized assignment and bounded outcomes.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.1--2.2) identify the balanced two-arm binary reduced experiment, and their Theorem 2.3 proves the two-arm bounded endpoint transfer that motivates the design-preserving three-arm proof here. Their Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C inform the one-dimensional Airy correction, but do not determine the labelled three-arm half-wedge constant or singular transverse bridge. The accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) supplies the lossless labelled eight-type reduction for binary schedules only. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof A.4) informs two-arm endpoint-game and posterior-mean constructions. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) supply general arm-labelled contrasts and unequal replication with linear unbiased estimation. Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) informs the first-order allocation square completion; Zhao and Ding (2023) and Li and Ding (2017) provide regular multi-arm finite-population asymptotics. Levit (1981) and Bickel (1981) inform the spectral route, while Aronow and Lopatto (2026, Theorems 1--3) impose design unbiasedness, which is not imposed here.
prose_updates.interpretation: Changing the measurement scale from binary endpoints to a common interval of width \(W\) multiplies every squared-error benchmark and allocation penalty by \(W^2\), but it does not change \(q^\star\), the \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation tolerance, or the dimensionless constant \(C_3\). The continuous bounded experiment is handled by Rao--Blackwellized endpoint randomization, not by pretending each bounded response is one of eight binary types.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded transfer is an exact equality of minimax values and a construction of a bounded estimator; it is not a literal finite-orbit representation of each continuous schedule. Within the binary game, the lower bound still fails if the posterior target is scalarized: the arm-labelled coefficient \(b_{A_i}(\alpha)\) and its residual-variance term are necessary. The unrestricted prior still needs its vanishing broad component to control linear allocation sensitivity. Finally, \(\eta=0\) is a minimizing singular fiber rather than a boundary of \(\mathbb R^2\); no transverse Laplacian or boundary condition is introduced.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The lossless labelled eight-type orbit reduction is inherited and applies literally to binary endpoint schedules. For every fixed finite common interval \([L,U]\), the new endpoint theorem proves only the exact minimax-value identities \(\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}=(U-L)^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}\) and \(\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=(U-L)^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\), together with explicit Rao--Blackwellized estimators and endpoint priors. The result does not claim a continuous-schedule eight-type likelihood, uniqueness of the unrestricted design, equality with fixed-count complete randomization, cellwise Le Cam equivalence, or exact finite-\(n\) saddle attainment. The singular bridge remains a two-sided comparison of minimax values, and the pooled-comparator check remains a restricted two-arm submodel rather than an equality of its Airy constant with \(C_3\).

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies the exact nonlinear binary endpoint gain; the proved bounded corollary transfers that gain, with squared-width scaling, to every common finite interval.
statement_notes.gap: The published two-arm theory gives neither the three-arm half-wedge eigenvalue \(-a_1'\) nor the singular labelled finite-orbit bridge; its bounded theorem also does not itself establish the three-arm transfer.
statement_notes.consumer: For an active treatment compared with two equally weighted comparators, the binary theorem and bounded corollary give the sharp worst-case MSE benchmark on any known common outcome interval.

statement_notes.justification: This inherited proposition is the literal exact reduction for binary endpoint schedules; the new endpoint theorem uses it only after proving a separate bounded minimax-value equality.
statement_notes.gap: It does not identify the likelihood orbit of a nonendpoint continuous schedule and is not presented as doing so.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the computable binary value that the bounded endpoint theorem rescales.

statement_notes.justification: The binary Airy rule and complete-schedule prior remain the core matching constructions; their Rao--Blackwellized and endpoint-pushforward versions are proved in \(\texttt{prop:bounded-matching-finite-n-constructions}\).
statement_notes.consumer: The bounded corollary converts these binary objects into an observed-data estimator and fixed-schedule prior for \([L,U]\)-valued outcomes.

statement_notes.justification: The binary frontier determines the allocation tolerance; exact endpoint transfer shows that bounded outcomes multiply its risk penalty by \((U-L)^2\) without changing the \(n^{-1/6}\) threshold.
statement_notes.consumer: Trial designers obtain the same allocation tolerance on any common bounded measurement scale.

statement_notes.justification: The existing proposition is a binary endpoint check. Its bounded counterpart uses the published Theorems 2.1--2.3 and explicitly distinguishes endpoint value transfer from a literal continuous-schedule orbit reduction.
statement_notes.consumer: The pair supplies binary and bounded regression tests for implementations while keeping the three-arm and restricted two-arm constants distinct.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem proves exact fixed-design and minimax equalities using endpoint inclusion and a valid Rao--Blackwellized observed-data rule.
statement_notes.gap: It generalizes the published two-arm endpoint transfer to the present zero-sum three-arm contrast and unrestricted schedule-independent design class.
statement_notes.consumer: Every binary sharp expansion, allocation comparison, estimator, and lower prior can be transported to a common bounded interval with the correct squared-width scaling.
